text: Diarrhoea ≤ 2 weeks

detail.problem: Per the briefing's convention ((< (onset X) (time_ago 3 days)) = onset within the last 3 days), (<= (onset Diarrhea) (time_ago 2 weeks)) reads 'diarrhoea for 2 weeks or less', which matches the page. Used consistently in all three left-branch rules.

The <=2 weeks branch is encoded with (<= (onset ...) (time_ago 2 weeks)), which per the briefing means onset at least 2 weeks ago (duration >= 2 weeks): reversed direction. Affects gastroenteritis, dysentery and cholera rules. Should be (> (onset ...) (time_ago 2 weeks)) or equivalent.

Encoded as (<= (onset Diarrhea) (time_ago 2 weeks)). If onset is a timestamp compared to the timestamp 'now minus 2 weeks', <= means the onset was 2 or more weeks ago, i.e. duration >= 2 weeks: the opposite of the page's '<= 2 weeks'. The page's branch needs onset within the last 2 weeks, i.e. (>= (onset ...) (time_ago 2 weeks)). The grammar does not document the direction, so confirm against the VHA evaluator; if it is reversed, the dysentery, gastroenteritis and cholera-by-flowchart rules all fire on chronic diarrhoea instead of acute. Also, duration is never asked (no check_for).
